messages:
Riley (oncall): Incident: sudden spike in errors for /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate, started ~10:12 UTC. 3x error rate, mix of 429 and 503. RTT tail increased ~2-3x. Traces show large queue depth on gpu-pool-2 and continuous batching backlog. Paging SRE now.
IncidentBot: Paging SRE rotation: Riley -> Priya at 10:13 UTC. Severity: P2 (customer impact, degraded but partially degraded).
Priya (sre): Confirming. I see a subset of clients (top 5) sending huge synchronous streaming requests for long prompts. Most of the volume is coming through the hosted API. Quick ask: can runtime drop non-essential streaming/graceful-streams for those clients as a short-term mitigation?
Jonas (runtime): We can apply per-customer shaping at the edge. Options: 1) Soft-rate-limit top offending API keys to 50% of their normal qps for 15m. 2) Disable streaming (fall back to non-streaming chunked responses) for requests > 8k tokens. Both are quick. Which to do first?
Riley (oncall): Do both in sequence: soft-rate-limit first (15m), then if error rate doesn't fall, force-disable streaming for long requests. Prioritize customers with highest token volume. Apply a 15m window and monitor.
Priya (sre): I'm applying the soft per-key shaping now via edge-config: `edgectl throttle --key-prefix pk_live_ --rate 0.5 --window 900s --reason "live-shape: embedding surge"`
IncidentBot: edgectl job 98321 queued -> applied to 5 keys.
Riley (oncall): Noted. Telemetry: keep an eye on 95/99th latency and queue_depth metric on gpu-pool-2. Alert me if 503s don't drop by 30% in 5m.
Jonas (runtime): Telemetry showing immediate reduction in queue depth ~18% after shaping. But still high 503s from one particular API key (pk_live_abc123). I'm toggling streaming-disable rule for that key to reduce KV cache pressure. Command: `edgectl config set pk_live_abc123 disable_streaming=true --duration 15m`
IncidentBot: config change applied for pk_live_abc123 (disable_streaming).
Nadia (sdk): Heads-up for client-side mitigations (we should push a short advisory and a library patch): recommended SDK changes for immediate client mitigations: 1) Switch to randomized exponential backoff with full jitter for retries. 2) Enforce idempotency tokens for any non-idempotent calls (uploads, fine-tune, multi-part generate). 3) Reduce concurrent default streaming connections per host from 8 -> 3 for hosted tier. I'll paste a quick config snippet.
Nadia (sdk): JS example (patch):
```
// new default retry config
const retryConfig = {
  maxRetries: 4,
  baseDelayMs: 200,    // base
  factor: 2,           // exponential
  jitter: 'full',      // randomized jitter
  maxDelayMs: 8000,
  retryOn: ['ECONNRESET','ETIMEDOUT','429','503']
}
client.configure({ retry: retryConfig, maxConcurrentStreams: 3 })
```
Nadia (sdk): Python example (patch):
```
retry = RetryConfig(max_retries=4, base=0.2, factor=2.0, max_backoff=8.0, jitter='full')
client = RedwoodClient(retry=retry, max_concurrent_streams=3)
```
Nadia (sdk): Idempotency guidance: require callers set `Idempotency-Key` header for any request that may create state; SDK will auto-generate a v4 UUID if absent and log a warning for 30 days. Server will treat duplicate idempotency keys as dedup attempt.
Sam (support): I'm drafting a customer advisory now. Key points: temporary shaping applied, please upgrade SDK or implement full-jitter exponential backoff, add idempotency keys where appropriate. I'll include a short troubleshooting checklist. Who owns the support msg?
Priya (sre): Support draft ok. Add note: "If you see persistent 503s after 20m of shaping, open a support ticket with sample request ids and timestamps; we'll whitelist if legitimate traffic is business-critical."
Riley (oncall): Also, immediate SDK patch release: bump patch version with default retry/jitter and concurrency cap. Nadia, can you publish a 0.5.1 hotfix and a short migration guide? Tag it as "mitigation release".
Nadia (sdk): Yes — preparing patch branch now. Will push release notes with code snippets and upgrade instructions. ETA 25 minutes.
Jonas (runtime): Runtime follow-up: we'll keep the per-key shaping on for 30m and then ramp back to 100% over 10m if signals are healthy. I'll also enable a temporary KV cache eviction policy for the affected pool to free memory: `runtime-admin set-evict-policy --pool gpu-pool-2 --percent 30 --ttl 60s`
IncidentBot: runtime-admin job 444-evict submitted -> completed.
Priya (sre): Monitoring: 503 rate down 42% overall, 95p latency down 25%. Still seeing 429 spikes for one outlier. I'll extend shaping for that key another 15m.
Riley (oncall): Good. Prepare a concise incident note for internal post-incident follow-up: root cause hypothesis = concentrated synchronous streaming/long-prompt load from a small set of clients increasing KV and batching pressure -> fallback to 503s. Action items: edge shaping, disable streaming for long requests, SDK retry/jitter patch, idempotency adoption, longer-term: quota + billing guardrails and better per-tenant telemetry.
Sam (support): Support advisory ready to go — sending in 5.
Nadia (sdk): Patch published 0.5.1-mitigation. Link: https://npm.redwood/sdk@0.5.1-mitigation (internal). Release notes include code examples and a note to set `Idempotency-Key`.
Priya (sre): Handoff: Riley -> Priya at 10:45 UTC for next shift monitoring. I'll keep the shaping extended until 11:15 UTC unless metrics are green.
Riley (oncall): Handoff ack. If anything regresses re-paging. Also please coordinate with product on any customers that need emergency increases.
Jonas (runtime): Leaving background task: gradual ramp-back job ready, will start only on green signals.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved to P2 -> mitigation stable at 11:05 UTC. Closing page but leaving follow-up ticket: INC-2026.
Riley (oncall): Thanks all. Follow-up actions assigned in INC-2026: SDK release verification, quota policy doc, postmortem draft.
Sam (support): Will notify affected customers about temporary shaping removal window once we ramp back.
Nadia (sdk): Will open an RFC for automatic idempotency token injection in SDKs and server-side idempotency tracking quotas.
Priya (sre): Leaving note: if we see similar patterns, consider automatic detection + auto-shape rule based on sustained token/sec per key.
Riley (oncall): End of thread — handing to Priya. :white_check_mark:
